Quick notes from an ops/bench perspective:
- Yes, we can simulate warmed vs cold KV cache. In the bench we run three modes: cold start, warmed (using a prefetched prefix set), and steady-state with TTL churn. Please indicate preferred warm-hit target (Ethan suggested 35–45%).
- For batching: we typically measure 3 profiles — latency-prioritized (batch size <= 8), balanced (<= 32), throughput (<= 128). We'll return tokens/$ by profile so you can pick the trade-off curve.
- Need to confirm concurrency envelope for your pilot (requests/sec). Bench accuracy depends on realistic concurrency and token-length distributions.

Karthik — any add on the model-variant/quantization assumptions we should include in the MAP?

Adding technical assumptions we should lock in before bench run:
- Model family / size: specify the candidate model(s) to use for the bench (e.g., Luma-13B int8 / Luma-70B q4). Different quantization will move tokens/$ materially.
- KV cache: define prefix-key granularity (sentence vs paragraph) — affects hit-rate modelling.
- Prefetch: if Luminar wants prefetching, we need an estimated prefetch ratio and the source TTL for cache entries. Prefetch increases throughput but also increases tokens served (cost).
- Batching policy: whether we allow time-based aggregation (max wait 15ms) vs size-only. Time-based batching can improve throughput without increasing user-visible latency much but complicates tail latency SLAs.

If you can confirm model variants and whether you want prefetch, we'll configure the 1k-sample bench accordingly.

Karthik
